newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says extending yield curve with new bond.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says extending yield curve with new bond.

text.p: Mexican state oil giant Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said on Wednesday that its latest Eurobond formed part of the company's plan to extend its yield curve.
"Pemex has achieved its objective of continuing to construct its yield curve, adding this operation to the two recent ones at five and seven years," the company said in a statement.
The 10-year, $250 million bond was issued earlier on Wednesday.
In March, Pemex issued a seven-year 350 billion lira floating-rate bond. That was followed in April with a five-year $300 million Eurobond.
The latest bond issue was bumped up from an originally planned $200 million.
"The issue was originally planned for $200 million, but we increased due to the strong demand on the part of institutional investors in United States, Asia and Europe," Pemex said.
The issue had an annual coupon of nine percent, and was priced at par. It had a yield equivalent to 223 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
The bond was placd by ABN Amro, Goldman Sachs and UBS, Pemex said.
